database.title: Database Storage
database.description: Local storage for sessions, trackers, and document history. PGLite is the current default; the faster SQLite backend is in alpha.
database.status_both: Both pglite-db/ and sqlite-db/ exist on disk.
database.status_pglite_only: pglite-db/ on disk; sqlite-db/ not yet created.
database.status_sqlite_only: sqlite-db/ on disk; legacy pglite-db/ absent.
database.snapshots_hint: Preserved snapshots on disk: {{count}}. The most recent will be used.
database.dry_run_description: Copies your data into a throwaway SQLite database alongside the live one, reports row counts and integrity, then deletes the temporary copy. Your real PGLite database is never touched. Available only while PGLite is active.
database.migrate_description_1: Moves all data from PGLite to SQLite. The original PGLite directory is preserved at
database.migrate_description_2: and can be restored from this panel.
database.migrated_description: Your data is already stored in the faster SQLite backend. No further migration is needed.
database.migration_warning: Migration runs without interruption and preserves the original PGLite directory for rollback.
database.adopt_dry_run: Switch to the dry-run SQLite copy
database.adopt_confirm:
Switch to the dry-run SQLite copy?

Nimbalyst will:
  1. Close the current PGLite database
  2. Copy anything new since the dry-run ({{age}} ago)
  3. Make SQLite the active backend
  4. Preserve the old PGLite for rollback

A relaunch is required after switching.
database.rollback_confirm: Restore the preserved PGLite database? You will lose any data created since the migration. Requires a relaunch.
database.preserve_and_switch: Preserving the previous PGLite directory and switching the active backend.
database.adopt_description: A successful dry-run from {{age}} is saved on disk ({{rows}} rows). Nimbalyst can promote it to be your active database — it will copy anything new since the dry-run, then switch the backend. The current PGLite directory is preserved for rollback.
database.switch_success: Switched to SQLite. Caught up {{rows}} new rows in {{duration}}. Please relaunch Nimbalyst for the change to take effect.
database.history_migration_warning: Migration completed with {{count}} document-history entries omitted. These entries are unavailable in history, but their original data is retained in a local recovery record. The original PGLite database is also retained. Sessions and messages were not skipped.

panel.restart_required: Database switch requires a restart. Nimbalyst will verify the database on the next startup.
panel.backend_description_both: Both pglite-db/ and sqlite-db/ exist on disk.
panel.backend_description_pglite: pglite-db/ on disk; sqlite-db/ not yet created.
panel.backend_description_sqlite: sqlite-db/ on disk; legacy pglite-db/ absent.
panel.dry_run_explanation: Copies your data into a temporary SQLite database alongside the live one, reports row counts and integrity, then keeps the successful copy for switching. Your real PGLite database is never touched. Available only while PGLite is active.
panel.migrate_description: Moves all your data from PGLite to SQLite. The original PGLite directory is preserved at
panel.migrate_description_suffix: and can be restored from this panel.
panel.already_migrated: Your data is already stored in the faster SQLite backend. No further migration is needed.
panel.rollback_description: Puts the most recent preserved PGLite copy back in front of the app. Data created since the migration will not be in it. The copies themselves are listed below.
panel.migration_flow_description: This runs in one uninterrupted flow and preserves the original PGLite directory for rollback.

recovery.title: Databases set aside on this computer
recovery.description: Earlier versions of Nimbalyst moved a database aside when opening it failed. These copies are kept indefinitely and are never removed automatically. A copy being here does not mean the database you are using now is damaged.
recovery.reason_candidate_missing: This copy is no longer on disk.
recovery.reason_already_resolved: You have already dealt with this copy.
recovery.reason_candidate_invalid: This copy is not a database Nimbalyst can read.
recovery.reason_candidate_not_richer: This copy does not appear to hold anything the current database is missing.
recovery.reason_candidate_unreadable: Nimbalyst could not read this copy well enough to describe it.
recovery.reason_live_unreadable: Nimbalyst could not read the current database, so it cannot compare the two.
recovery.reason_facts_changed: The files changed while Nimbalyst was reading them, so it stopped rather than compare a moving target.
recovery.reason_both_have_content: This copy and the current database both hold data. Nimbalyst cannot tell which one you want.
recovery.reason_live_empty_new: The current database is empty, and this computer has no project history to compare it against.
recovery.reason_live_empty_established: The current database is empty, but this computer has settings for projects you have used, and this copy holds data.
recovery.reason_unknown: Nimbalyst has no description for this result.
recovery.offer_title: One of these copies may hold data your current database does not
recovery.offer_review: Review it below before deciding anything.
recovery.restored: Restored from {{name}}. The database that was live before this, and the copy it was restored from, are both still on disk. Relaunch Nimbalyst to use the restored database.
recovery.rolled_back: The database you were using has been put back, and every copy is still on disk.
recovery.not_changed: The database you were using was not changed, and every copy is still on disk.
recovery.cannot_restore_sqlite: This build cannot restore a PGLite copy onto a SQLite database. You can still open the copy in Finder and keep it.
recovery.confirm_description: Read what each copy becomes. Nimbalyst does not delete any of them, now or later.
recovery.copy_unchanged: The copy above, unchanged. Restoring reads it; it is never modified.
recovery.snapshot_kept: A snapshot of the database you are using now, taken and verified before anything moves, saved beside it with pre-restore and a timestamp in its name.
recovery.displaced_kept: The database you are using now, moved aside with displaced and a timestamp in its name.
recovery.restore_safety: The copy is verified before it replaces anything. If verification or any later step fails, the database you are using now stays in place and every copy remains on disk. Nimbalyst must be relaunched afterwards either way.
recovery.ack_restore: I have read which database is replaced and which copies are kept.

migration_state.reason_backup_larger: A database set aside on this computer is much larger than the one in use, so Nimbalyst will not copy the one in use without you looking first.
migration_state.reason_projects_without_sessions: This computer has settings for projects you have opened, but the database Nimbalyst would copy from has no sessions in it.
migration_state.reason_source_unreadable: Nimbalyst could not read the database it would copy from, and an unreadable database is not treated as an empty one.
migration_state.reason_source_missing: The database Nimbalyst would copy from is not on disk.
migration_state.reason_insufficient_disk: There is not enough free disk space to hold both databases during the copy.
migration_state.reason_unknown: Nimbalyst recorded a reason it cannot describe in this build.
migration_state.blocked_title: Automatic migration is held back on this computer
migration_state.recorded: Recorded {{date}}. Nimbalyst re-checks this on its own if what it measures changes. Nothing has been copied, moved, or deleted.
migration_state.clear_description: Clearing this lets a later launch assess the migration again. It does not start a migration and does not change any data, but it does remove the check that stopped Nimbalyst from copying a database it could not confirm was the one holding your work. Look at any set-aside copies first.
migration_state.clear_button: Clear this and re-check on the next launch
migration_state.copies_title: PGLite copies kept from a migration
migration_state.copies_description: A migration keeps the PGLite database it copied from. These stay until you remove them; Nimbalyst does not delete them on a schedule.
migration_state.rollback_source: This is the copy "Restore from preserved PGLite" would use.
migration_state.not_rollback_source: Kept on disk. It is not the copy a rollback would use.
migration_state.delete_description: This permanently removes {{size}} — the PGLite database as it stood on {{date}}, before it was migrated. Sessions and document history that exist only in this copy cannot be recovered afterwards.
migration_state.delete_rollback_warning: This is the copy a rollback restores from. Once it is gone, this install cannot be put back onto PGLite.
migration_state.current_db_untouched: The database you are using now is not touched.
migration_state.ack_delete: I understand this copy cannot be recovered after deleting it.
